calls.head: Crash the net vs. bombs away
calls.body: The Mammoth get in close, but the Avalanche mostly shoot from distance. Utah is one of the league’s best for shots from in close, and Colorado is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Mammoth to do more of their damage around the net.

story.head: The Mammoth end a six-game winless run
paras: The Mammoth won for the first time in seven games, after going 0-3-3. Early in the second, Liam O'Brien got the scoring started for the Mammoth, and Jack McBain and Gabriel Landeskog squared off. Vincent Trocheck made it 2-0 for the Mammoth on the power play late in the second. Alex Gagne and O'Brien fought later in the period. Dmitri Simashev stretched the lead to 3-0 shorthanded early in the third, with Trocheck picking up his 400th NHL assist on the goal. Parker Kelly got the Avalanche on the board with just under five minutes left, and Kevin Stenlund added an empty-net goal with just over two minutes left to make it 4-1.

The Mammoth drove the play, and the scoreboard caught up. Sebastian Cossa, who gave up five goals in Vegas in his last start, made 30 saves for the Mammoth, and Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 25 of 28 at the other end. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Kailer Yamamoto, by our Swing measure.
The Mammoth killed all four Avalanche power plays. The Mammoth improved to 11-9-3, fifth in the Central, while the Avalanche dropped to 12-7-3, third in the Central.

items.text: The Avalanche’s five-game point streak is over.

The Mammoth won without Nate Schmidt, John Marino, Nick Schmaltz and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Avalanche and the Senators were missing more at the time.
Liam O'Brien scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 4 (14 games played since).
With Nathan MacKinnon out, Brock Nelson took his spot, though he won only 5 of 24 faceoffs.
